proposed_widenings.name: create_extradimensional_space
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell's primary mechanic is creating a temporary extradimensional refuge that creatures can voluntarily enter and exit. No v4 atom covers this: transport_exile forces involuntary exile, container_storage is for item containers with carrying-capacity semantics, and block_travel/block_targeting have no anchor point to attach to since the space itself is what needs to be represented. A new atom is needed to model a spell-created extradimensional space with: a physical entry point (rope top), creature capacity (8 medium-or-smaller), bidirectional effect blocking (nothing passes in or out), and a timed duration.
proposed_widenings.evidence: At the rope's upper end, an Invisible 3-foot-by-5-foot portal opens to an extradimensional space that lasts until the spell ends. That space can be reached by climbing the rope. The space can hold up to eight Medium or smaller creatures. Attacks, spells, and other effects can't pass into or out of the space, but creatures inside it can see through the portal.

proposed_widenings.name: block_travel / block_targeting scoped to a created space
proposed_widenings.justification: The blocking of attacks/spells/effects passing in or out of the space could reuse block_travel and block_targeting, but both atoms currently attach to a creature or area attachment. Rope Trick needs these to attach to the extradimensional space itself (a new attachment target), bidirectionally. This is a secondary widening that depends on the create_extradimensional_space atom being available first.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Attacks, spells, and other effects can't pass into or out of the space.

notes: The spell family is clear (activation spell, direct phase, object attachment on the rope, timed 1-hour non-concentration duration). The family itself exists. The blocker is the absence of any atom for creating a temporary extradimensional refuge. transport_exile has wrong directionality and semantics (involuntary, one-way), container_storage has wrong context (item-held storage, not walk-in inhabited space), and block_travel/block_targeting have no anchor to attach to without the space being a first-class atom. The 'creatures can see through the portal' and 'capacity: 8' sub-mechanics are also unrepresented but are secondary to the missing primary atom.
